issues.failure_explanation: In the hierarchical split, the SWE contribution does not vanish: with the full SWME entropy variables, \jump{w}^T f^{EC,SWE} - \avg{w^T B^{SWE}}\jump{u} = -\sum_j \avg{hu_m}\avg{\alpha_j}\jump{\alpha_j}/(2j+1) \neq 0, because w_1 contains -\tfrac12\sum_j \alpha_j^2/(2j+1) while f^{EC,SWE} has first component \avg{hu_m} (e.g., states u_m=1, h=1, b=0, \alpha_1:0\to2 give -2/3). Thus eq:entropy_conservation_condition_swe is false as stated and dropping the SWE block in eq:leftside:EC:linearity is unjustified. Simultaneously, the first equality of eq:leftside:EC:P omits the term +\sum_j \jump{\alpha_j}\avg{hu_m}\avg{\alpha_j}/(2j+1) produced by contracting the \avg{hu_m}\avg{\boldsymbol\alpha} entry of \bar f^{EC,SWE} with \jump{w_{j+2}}=\jump{\alpha_j}/(2j+1). The two errors cancel exactly (via \jump{\alpha_j}\avg{\alpha_j}=\tfrac12\jump{\alpha_j^2}, the identity the paper itself states), so the final EC identity and the theorem statement are correct, but the two intermediate displays are false as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the bookkeeping in the proof: state that the SWE block contributes -\sum_j \avg{hu_m}\avg{\alpha_j}\jump{\alpha_j}/(2j+1) (not zero) and include the omitted +\sum_j \jump{\alpha_j}\avg{hu_m}\avg{\alpha_j}/(2j+1) term in the bar-SWE computation, noting the two cancel; no change to any statement is required.
issues.overall_effect: Two displayed steps of the proof of Theorem thm:ec_flux are false; since they cancel, the entropy-conservation property of the flux eq:f:EC (verified independently by direct algebra) and all downstream results (ES scheme eq:es_dgsem, well-balancedness lemma:well_balancedness) remain valid.
issues.title: EC-flux proof: SWE block does not vanish and a cancelling moment term is omitted in the bar-SWE computation (the two errors cancel)
issues.why_classification: The theorem and every downstream guarantee survive; the repair is a short, local algebraic correction of the proof's decomposition requiring no new lemma, construction, or argument.

issues.failure_explanation: Direct inversion of the entropy Hessian gives H_E^{-1} = (1/g)(y y^T + diag(0, gh, 3gh, ..., (2N+1)gh)): the first entry of the diagonal part is 0, not 1. With the stated z = (1, gh, 3gh, ...), \bar H_{11} = 2/g, so \bar H is not the inverse Hessian at any state, and the claimed relation fails already in the first component: (1/g)(\avg{y}^T\jump{w} + \jump{w_1}) = \jump{h} + (1/g)\jump{w_1} \neq \jump{h}. Concrete counterexample (N=0, constant b): states (h,hu)=(1,0) and (2,0) give \jump{w}=(g,0)^T and (\bar H\jump{w})_1 = 2 \neq 1 = \jump{h}. The claim characterizing the dissipation matrix in eq:es_fluctuation_definition is therefore false as written.

failure_location.quote: with vectors $\mbf{y} = (1, u_m, \bB{\alpha}^{\rm T})^{\rm T}$ and $\mbf{z} = (1, gh, 3gh, \dots, (2n+1)gh)^{\rm T}$ is the positive definite inverse of the Hessian of the entropy function $\mathbb{E}\big((h, hu_m, h\bB{\alpha}^{\rm T})\big)$, evaluated at some intermediate state $\bar{\bB{u}} \in [\bB{u}^-, \bB{u}^+]$, that for  constant bottom topography satisfies the relation $\text{diag}(\bar{\mbf{H}}, 1) \jump{\bB{w}} = \jump{\bB{u}}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the first entry of z from 1 to 0, i.e., z = (0, gh, 3gh, ..., (2N+1)gh); then \bar H is exactly the inverse Hessian at the arithmetically averaged state and the relation diag(\bar H,1)\jump{w}=\jump{u} holds for constant bottom topography (componentwise verification uses only \jump{ab}=\avg a\jump b+\jump a\avg b). Alternatively, keep the matrix and delete the inverse-Hessian/relation claim.
issues.overall_effect: Only the characterization of \bar H and the exact relation to \jump{u} are false. Entropy stability of the scheme eq:es_dgsem is unaffected (the cited ES argument uses only positive definiteness of \bar H, which holds), and well-balancedness (lemma:well_balancedness) is unaffected (it uses \jump{w}=0 on the first N+2 components at lake-at-rest).
issues.title: Dissipation matrix \bar H is not the inverse entropy Hessian and the claimed relation diag(\bar H,1)\jump{w}=\jump{u} fails
issues.why_classification: A one-entry correction makes every stated property true; no theorem, scheme, or guarantee is changed or lost, and no new argument is needed.
